resources.string: Measures your speaker with the phone\'s microphone, or looks up the published measurements of your speaker or headphones, and makes an AxionFx preset in the sound style you pick.
Neutral and true to the recording
Fuller bass and softer highs, relaxed
Deep thump, punchy and loud, sounds like a much bigger speaker
As much bass as the speaker can take
Clear voices for podcasts, films and calls
Your own preset\'s sound: big warm bass, tube warmth, exciter and clarity for bite
Your own preset\'s sound on any headphones: big warm bass kept tight by tube, exciter and clarity
Neutral: the target the headphones were measured against
Fuller low end and softer highs for long listening
Club sub-bass you feel, smooth highs, loud and big
Deep rumble down to 25 Hz, as much as they can take
Clear voices for podcasts, films and calls
Type the model of your headphones, earbuds or speaker to tune from its published measurements, without measuring. Headphones from AutoEq, speakers from spinorama.org.
e.g. Galaxy Buds, AirPods Pro, JBL Flip
Downloading the list of models… (once, a few MB)
No model matches \"%1$s\". Try fewer words, or measure it below.
%1$d more: type more of the name
Tuned from the published curve of %1$s. Pick another style above at any time.
For speakers that aren\'t listed, or to include your room
Top is the earpiece mic. Point it at the speaker. If one of the phone\'s mics is broken, pick the other one.
Normal suits most speakers. Pick Quiet if it says the mic overloaded.
More tests average out noise and the room. Move the phone a hand\'s width between tests; there\'s a short countdown to do it.
Used for the preset\'s file name
Connect the speaker and set it to a normal listening volume.
In AxionFx, turn the main switch off so the bare speaker is measured.
Put the phone about 1 m in front of the speaker at ear height, the chosen mic facing it.
Keep the room quiet. Each test sweeps a tone from low to high for about 11 seconds.
Shaded: below what the speaker can play. EQ can\'t add bass there, so it\'s cut instead to keep the woofer clean.
Published curve, leveled to its mids. Shaded: below what it can play.
Tuned for headphones: sub-bass on the FIR EQ\'s 25 and 40 Hz bands, and gentler highs because they play right at your ear (peaks are cut, dips only nudged, no exciter or clarity).
FIR EQ sub cut: 25 Hz %1$.0f dB, 40 Hz %2$.0f dB
FIR EQ sub-bass: 25 Hz %1$+.1f dB, 40 Hz %2$+.1f dB
To use it: AxionFx → Presets → Import, pick the file from Download/AxionFx, load it and turn AxionFx back on. You can switch the style above and save again without measuring again.
Turn AxionFx off first and tick the box, otherwise its effects end up in the measurement.
The microphone permission is needed to measure.
The chosen microphone hears almost nothing. Try another microphone or turn the speaker up.
Too loud: the microphone overloaded. Pick a quieter test tone or turn the speaker down, then measure again.
